findings.title: Clauses (h), (i) and (e) of orca-browser-agent-live turn a failed CLI read into 'not listed' or 'not visible', which passes
findings.description: listIds() and cookieNames() return [] when the CLI call fails (r.ok false). Clause (h), user close (A7): listedAfter becomes false on the first failed `tab list`, and the clause passes. Clause (i), reload: oldPages is read through listIds before the reload. If that call fails, oldPages is [] and oldListed stays [], so the 'old pages still listed' assertion checks nothing. Clause (e), container: userVisible comes from a second `cookie get` on the agent page. If that call fails, the user cookie counts as not visible. The earlier ownRead positive read used a different call. These clauses guard tab scope and container isolation: a closed or reloaded tab must not remain addressable, and an agent must not read the user's cookies.
findings.scenario: After the reload in (i), orcad answers `tab list --worktree W` with runtime_error, for example because the host session is mid re-attach. oldPages=[] (or now=[] on every poll), oldListed=[], and verdictReload reports no old pages. In (h), a stale page that is still listed passes whenever `tab list` fails at that moment. In (e), if the agent's second cookie get is refused with an error, userVisible=false and the clause passes.
findings.evidence:
scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:395 `const listIds = (r) => (r.ok ? (r.result?.tabs ?? []).map((t) => t.browserPageId) : []);`
:396 `const cookieNames = (r) => (r.ok ? ... : []);`
:938 `for (let i = 0; i < 20 && listedAfter; i++) { ... listedAfter = listIds(await ctx.cli('tab', 'list', '--worktree', W)).includes(page); }`
:969 `const oldPages = listIds(await ctx.cli('tab', 'list', '--worktree', W));`
:975 `oldListed = oldPages.filter((p) => now.includes(p));`
:882 `userVisible: cookieNames(await ctx.cli('cookie', 'get', '--page', page)).includes('pbuser')`
findings.suggested_fix: Record the CLI outcome alongside the list. Make a failed `tab list` or `cookie get` red ('instrument failed'). Require oldPages to be non-empty and to contain the (a)/(j) page ids before the reload. Require the user-close poll to have seen the page listed once before the close. Add self-test plants for each case.
findings.preconditions: An orcad or CLI error at the moment of the read. A regression that fails the read and leaves the page listed passes.

votes.reasoning: At line 395, listIds maps a failed CLI result (r.ok false) to [], and cookieNames at 396 does the same. Clause (h), line 937-938: the loop stops at the first failed `tab list`, listedAfter becomes false, and verdictUserClose (248-251) passes. Clause (i): oldPages (969) comes from listIds. If that call fails, oldListed starts as [] and the loop never runs. If any later poll returns [] from an error, oldListed becomes []. verdictReload (253-259) checks only oldListed.length and has no 'oldPages was read' positive control. Clause (e): userVisible (882) is a separate cookie get. A failure counts as not visible, and verdictContainer (182-186) passes, because ownRead is an earlier, independent call. No caller validates r.ok for these reads. The only runtime element is the CLI error itself, which is the stated precondition, not an unresolved step in the code path.
votes.guard_or_evidence: scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:395-396, 882, 937-938, 969-975; verdictReload/verdictUserClose/verdictContainer have no read-succeeded control

findings.title: Self-tests leave many live-row assertions without a planted fault
findings.description: The project rule requires a planted fault per assertion. The following assertions have none. orca-browser-agent-live: verdictActs (b) has no plant at all (title, click count, typed value). verdictRenderer is planted only for lease_stale (not placement kind, createPage not arrived, or missing credential). verdictReload is planted only for agentWidgetsAfter (not reattached, oldListed). verdictScreenshot: deviceDpr mismatch, outside pixel red. verdictDecoy: createOk, title, quietMs. verdictAuth: authorized. verdictLogins: agentSubmitted. verdictCreate: !agent, boundTab. verdictNoPane: newTabs>1, ms>CREATE_MS. verdictTyping: chrome focus moved. verdictActivation: user focus changed, !bound. verdictFirstDocument: !created. verdictContainer: userCookieSet. verdictRefusals: missing error.code. orca-agent-mark-live: Stop button missing, empty baseline, stopped.mark and stopped.stopped. orca-agent-status-live: bridgeDir empty, launcher not naming the bridge folder, wrapper missing, engine 'does not descend from the terminal daemon', 'no agent process', quit 'vacuous'. orca-service-live: reap 'old daemon alive', 'state not ready'.
findings.scenario: An edit inverts `if (o.authorized)` in verdictAuth, or deletes the verdictActs title comparison. The self-test still prints PASS, because no plant reaches those lines.

findings.title: Assertions that cannot fire in a live run: (l) capturedAfter and status-live waitingNotDerivable
findings.description: verdictLogins reds on capturedAfter > 0, a count of stored logins for 'pbagent' after the agent submit. Gecko's form-submit capture only offers a save doorhanger. A login is stored only if a user accepts it, so the count stays 0 even when the agent tab has a working LoginManager actor. The agentActor assertion is the only effective one. In orca-agent-status-live, agentVerdict reds when waitingNotDerivable is set while derivedWaitingEvent names an event. The live caller passes waitingNotDerivable: !derivedWaitingEvent, so the condition is always false.
findings.scenario: The agent container wall regresses so that an agent-typed submit triggers capture. No login is stored without an accepted doorhanger, so capturedAfter stays 0 and only agentActor can catch it. The status-live branch is unreachable in any live run.
findings.evidence:
scripts/verify-orca-browser-agent-live.mjs:203 `if (o.capturedAfter > 0) ...`; 455 `capturedAfter: await countLogins(ctx, 'pbagent')`
scripts/verify-orca-agent-status-live.mjs:124 `if (obs.waitingNotDerivable) fails.push(...)` and 281 `waitingNotDerivable: !derivedWaitingEvent`
findings.suggested_fix: For (l), observe the capture attempt directly, for example a password-save doorhanger or a PasswordManager:onFormSubmit message for the agent browser. findings.title: The harness rewrites the owner's real ~/.claude/.credentials.json with a read-then-rename that can lose a concurrent write
findings.description: scratchSignInSettled() reads the real credentials file, compares hashes, writes a temp file and renames it over the real file, keeping the other keys from the earlier read. Nothing locks against the owner's own claude processes, which write the same file (token refresh, MCP OAuth entries) between the read and the rename. A write that lands in that window is overwritten. The sweep in liveHome() also runs this write-back for every stale pb-home-* folder at the start of any live row. So rows that never seed a sign-in (credential-store, service, browser-agent) can also write the real credential store.
findings.scenario: During a live run, the owner's interactive claude session adds an MCP server OAuth token to ~/.claude/.credentials.json. The harness then disposes a scratch HOME whose token rotated: it read `real` before that write and renames {...real, claudeAiOauth: rotated} over the file. The MCP token is lost, and the owner must re-authenticate that server.

scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:108-119 `const real = realFile ? readJson(realFile) : {}; ... writeFileSync(tmp, JSON.stringify({ ...real, claudeAiOauth: rotated }), ...); renameSync(tmp, realFile);`
:144-147 sweep `if (name.startsWith('pb-home-') && !homeInUse(dir)) disposeHome(dir);`
findings.suggested_fix: Re-read the real file immediately before the rename and abort if its mtime or contents changed. Better, never write the real store: keep the scratch folder and print the instruction (the existing fallback). Limit the sweep's write-back to rows that seeded a sign-in.
findings.preconditions: A rotated token in a scratch HOME and a concurrent write to the real credentials file.

votes.reasoning: In scratchSignInSettled (scripts/lib/firefox-bidi.mjs:103-129), the real ~/.claude/.credentials.json is read at :109. The compare-and-swap at :112 checks only that claudeAiOauth.refreshToken still hashes to the seeded value. Then {...real, claudeAiOauth: rotated} is written to a temp file and renamed over the real file (:116-117). No lock is held, and the file is not re-read before the rename. A concurrent write by the owner's own claude process (an MCP OAuth entry, or any key other than the refresh token) that lands between the read at :109 and the rename at :117 is lost. The window is short: it is all synchronous calls, on the order of milliseconds. Claude's own writers use the same read-modify-write pattern. The sweep in liveHome (:144-147) calls disposeHome, and so this write-back, for every stale pb-home-* folder whose .pid is dead. So any row that calls liveHome can write the real file, but only when a folder left by an earlier SIGKILLed seeded run holds a rotated token. The preconditions (a rotated token in a scratch HOME plus a concurrent write inside a millisecond window) make this low.

The driver counts any exit 0 as PASS, so the verify-uri-roundtrip row (full tier, via check_verify_uri_roundtrip) stays green. findings.title: orca-repin workflow rule asserts nothing when bump-pr-orca or detect-orca is renamed or removed
findings.description: The orca-repin rule enforces several App-token ordering invariants in release-train.yml: the token is minted only after the --replay-only replay and the explicit-path git add, no Orca code (pnpm, corepack, tsc, build-orca.sh) runs in the job that holds the token, the job only arms auto-merge, and TAG and COMMIT are re-checked before use. Every clause sits under `if (bump !== undefined && bump !== null)`, keyed on the literal job id. Rename the job (for example to bump-orca or orca-bump-pr), or move these steps into another job, and the rule is silent: no clause fails and nothing asserts that the bump job exists. The ORCA_CODE scan also covers bump-pr-orca alone, so a new job that mints the bot App token and runs pnpm on the fetched Orca tree is not checked by this rule. detect-orca has the same existence guard.
findings.scenario: A refactor renames bump-pr-orca to bump-orca and moves the 'Mint the bot App token' step above the 'Replay the pin move' step, which clones the tagged upstream Orca tree. That is the P68-35 exposure: the token exists while code from a possibly compromised upstream tag (actor f) is present in the job. scripts/verify-workflows.mjs passes and the workflows row stays green in --quick.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-workflows.mjs:1086-1087 `const bump = jobs['bump-pr-orca']; if (bump !== undefined && bump !== null) { ... mint < replay ... ORCA_CODE ... }` and :1112-1113 `const det = jobs['detect-orca']; if (det !== undefined && det !== null) {`. No else branch and no existence assertion. The orca-repin self-test plants edit only the existing job and never remove or rename it.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail when release-train.yml has no bump-pr-orca or detect-orca job while scripts/fetch-orca.sh is tracked (derive the expectation from the tree). Better, identify the bump job structurally: any job that both mints the App token and runs rebase-orca.sh or touches orca/. Apply the ORCA_CODE scan to every job that mints an App token. Add plants that rename the job and require red.
findings.preconditions: A workflow refactor renames or splits the Orca bump job.

votes.reasoning: In scripts/verify-workflows.mjs:1086-1087 every orca-repin clause (mint-after-replay/add ordering, ORCA_CODE scan, --auto, TAG/COMMIT re-check) sits inside `if (bump !== undefined && bump !== null)` keyed on the literal 'bump-pr-orca'. detect-orca has the same existence guard at :1112-1113. There is no else branch, and I found no job-set pinning for release-train.yml in the script. The header comment at :141 states the rule applies 'when bump-pr-orca exists', so skipping a missing job is deliberate. A rename or split therefore removes these assertions without a red. Generic rules (issues-write, app-token-inputs, dry-run-gate) still apply to a renamed job. None of them checks mint ordering against the Orca replay or Orca code execution in the token-holding job, so the P68-35 ordering is no longer checked. It needs a maintainer workflow edit, which goes through review.

findings.title: Release licence-rulings guard is checked only for position: continue-on-error or '|| true' on it stays green, and the Windows guard is not checked at all
findings.description: Rule 12 (P68-21: no release carries Orca's closure while an owner licence ruling is pending) checks only that a step whose run text contains `scripts/verify-licence-allowlist.mjs --rulings` comes before the build-orca.sh step in build-linux. The rulings step is not passed through failOpenFaults(), which the script applies to the SHA gate, the key gate and the purge step. A `continue-on-error: true`, an `|| true`, a `set +e` or a changed `if:` on it defeats the guard with rule 12 still green. The same guard in build-windows (release.yml:576-582) is checked by no rule in verify-release-shape.mjs or verify-build-windows-shape.mjs, because neither file mentions 'rulings' outside rule 12's build-linux scope.
findings.scenario: An edit adds `continue-on-error: true` under 'Refuse to build while an Orca licence ruling is pending (P68-21)' in release.yml build-linux, so builds go ahead while the bundled SDK's terms check is pending. Or it deletes the build-windows copy of the step. release-shape and build-windows-shape both stay PASS, and the release ships Orca's closure with a ruling open.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-release-shape.mjs:560 `const rulingsAt = at(/\bscripts\/verify-licence-allowlist\.mjs --rulings\b/);` :566 `if (rulingsAt.length === 0 || rulingsAt[0] > orcaAt[0]) fail(...)`. There is no failOpenFaults(buildSteps[rulingsAt[0]]). Compare :263 and :281, which apply failOpenFaults to the gate steps. grep -n rulings scripts/verify-build-windows-shape.mjs returns nothing; release.yml:582 holds the Windows copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply failOpenFaults(step, "steps.key_gate.outputs.build == 'true'") to the rulings step. Add the same position and fail-open rule for build-windows in verify-build-windows-shape.mjs. Add plants for continue-on-error, '|| true' and removal of the Windows guard.
findings.preconditions: An edit to release.yml weakens or removes the guard step.

votes.reasoning: Partly confirmed. For build-linux, rule 12 (scripts/verify-release-shape.mjs:560-566) checks only that the --rulings step exists and comes before build-orca.sh. That step is never passed to failOpenFaults, so `continue-on-error: true`, `|| true` or `set +e` on it stays green. A changed `if:` is caught, contrary to the claim: every build-linux step after key_gate must carry exactly KEY_IF (verify-release-shape.mjs:284-288). For build-windows, weakening the step is also caught: verify-build-windows-shape.mjs:343-349 runs failOpenFaults over every build-windows step (continue-on-error, `|| true`, `set +e`, a wrong `if:`). Only deleting the Windows rulings step (release.yml:576-582) goes unchecked, because no rule requires a --rulings step in build-windows. The remaining gaps are continue-on-error, `|| true` or `set +e` on the Linux step, and deletion of the Windows step. findings.title: Quick-tier checks for bundled extensions, the bundled XPI and Orca licences skip their substantive legs in CI and still exit PASS
findings.description: These scripts print one SKIP line for each leg whose input is not on disk, then exit 0, and the driver counts exit 0 as PASS. verify.yml runs --quick over a built Theia with no fetched orca/ and no .mozbuild/bundled-xpi cache. In that setting: (1) bundled-xpi skips the cached XPI's sha256, manifest id and version, signature presence, and the D-85 endpoint leg (every default-on uBlock filter-list host must have an allow row); (2) bundled-extensions skips the Orca pnpm-lock equality leg (verify-bundled-extensions.mjs:120) and possibly the LICENSE quotation leg (:126); (3) licence-allowlist skips the per-package Orca licence rule (verify-licence-allowlist.mjs:502), the bundled XPI licence line (:303) and the LICENSE digests of absent trees (:115). Each SKIP is named, but in --quick and CI these legs never go red. stage-bundled-xpi.sh re-checks sha256 when it stages, and rebase-orca.sh runs licence-allowlist with SKIP treated as red, so integrity has other guards. The D-85 endpoint-allowlist leg and the SDK lock-equality leg have none in CI.
findings.scenario: A uBlock pin bump adds a new default-on filter-list host. powerbrowser/endpoint-allowlist.json gets no allow row, and the shipped browser contacts an unlisted host with no user action. CI --quick prints 'verify-bundled-xpi: SKIP -- uBlock0@raymondhill.net: no cached ...' and 'PASS -- the pins are well formed'. The gap appears only on a developer host that has staged the XPI.
findings.evidence: scripts/verify-bundled-xpi.mjs:212-214 `if (!existsSync(xpi)) { skips.push(...); continue; }` and report() at :590-597 exits 0 with skips. scripts/verify-bundled-extensions.mjs:120 `if (orca === null) skips.push(...)`. scripts/verify-licence-allowlist.mjs:502 `if (d.skip) pr.skips.push(...)`. .github/workflows/verify.yml:83-93 builds Theia and runs --quick with no fetch-orca or stage-bundled-xpi step.
findings.suggested_fix: Either stage the pinned XPI in verify.yml (the download is sha256-pinned) so the cached legs run in CI, or give a SKIP its own exit code that the driver reports as SKIP, and make --gate refuse a SKIP for rows whose input CI can produce. At minimum, derive the endpoint leg's host set from a tracked copy of assets.json, so it does not depend on the cache.
findings.preconditions: Runs where the cache, orca/ or the built extension copy is absent, which is the CI --quick configuration.

votes.reasoning: In scripts/verify-bundled-xpi.mjs:210-214, staticLeg() skips the digest, manifest, signature and D-85 endpoint legs whenever .mozbuild/bundled-xpi/<id>-<version>.xpi is absent. report() at :590-597 exits 0 when there are only skips. .github/workflows/verify.yml:79-93 fetches upstream, builds Theia and runs --quick, with no fetch-orca or stage-bundled-xpi step. release.yml stages the XPI inside package-linux.sh, but its packaged-rows loop (release.yml:207-213) does not run bundled-xpi, and the bundled-xpi-packaged leg (checkPackagedDir, :119-132) checks file set and sha256 only, not endpoints. So the endpoint-allowlist leg runs only on a host that has staged the cache. verify-bundled-extensions.mjs:120 and :126 and verify-licence-allowlist.mjs:502 skip in the same way when orca/ is absent. Each skip is named in the output. The pin bump that triggers the scenario normally happens on a developer host that downloads and stages the XPI, and rebase-orca.sh treats a SKIP as red. That keeps this at hardening level.

findings.description: Lane-merge scaffolding that is still in place: when no file under theia/extensions/orca-browser/src exists, the kinds parity, push parity and privileged-kind rules leave out webTabAgent, webTabAgentStop and agentControlChanged. orca-browser is merged now, so the exemption is off. findings.title: Windows native check exempts every i386 .exe outside orca/, not just the NSIS helper
findings.description: The comment justifies one exception, the NSIS uninstall/helper.exe, which is 32-bit by design. isInstallerHelper instead exempts any .exe outside orca/ whose PE machine is 0x014c, other than node.exe and rg.exe, wherever it sits in the stage. No self-test case shows that an i386 .exe at another path (for example under the Theia sidecar) still goes red, or that helper.exe is exempted (a positive control).
findings.scenario: The Windows sidecar stage picks up a 32-bit tool, for example sidecar/lib/foo.exe built for the wrong arch. package-target-natives for win64 filters it out as an 'installer helper' and passes, although the comment's rule is that only the NSIS helper may be i386.

The path is never compared to uninstall/helper.exe. checkTree (:150) drops every such file from the native universe for a PE target, so an i386 sidecar/lib/foo.exe in a win64 stage is never examined and the row can stay green. The comment at :82 names uninstall/helper.exe. The header comment at :15-17 states the wider rule, so the code follows its own header, but nothing ties the exemption to the helper's location. One part of the finding is wrong: a positive control does exist. At :332-341 the self-test plants exe-names/uninstall-helper.exe as i386 and requires that it is not examined. The i386 plants are i386.node at :309 (not .exe) and orca/out/orcad/helper.exe at :366 (inside orca/). The self-test would therefore stay green if the exemption were widened further. This is a hardening gap in an architecture check, not a security boundary.

findings.title: Snapshot fixture generator runs the pinned agent-browser with the developer's full environment and HOME config
findings.description: The generator runs orca/node_modules/agent-browser (third-party, from the Orca pin) with { ...process.env }, so every AGENT_BROWSER_* variable in the developer's shell (PROFILE, AUTO_CONNECT, INIT_SCRIPTS, EXTENSIONS, PROXY, CONFIG) and ~/.agent-browser/config.json under the real HOME apply to the run. The committed reference fixtures, which verify-orca-browser-snapshot-live compares PowerBrowser's snapshot against, then depend on ambient configuration. A set AGENT_BROWSER_AUTO_CONNECT or AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE drives the developer's real browser profile, not a fresh Chromium.
findings.scenario: The developer's shell exports AGENT_BROWSER_INIT_SCRIPTS (or config.json sets one) that injects DOM. The regenerated <page>.json fixtures carry the injected nodes, they are committed, and the snapshot parity row compares against a format no clean agent-browser produces. Alternatively, AGENT_BROWSER_AUTO_CONNECT=1 attaches to the user's running Chrome and opens the fixture pages in it.
findings.evidence: scripts/gen-orca-snapshot-fixtures.mjs:93 `const env = { ...process.env, AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH: chromium };` passed to execFile(process.execPath, [AB_LAUNCHER, '--session', session, ...]) at :97. orca/node_modules/agent-browser/README.md documents AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE, AGENT_BROWSER_AUTO_CONNECT, AGENT_BROWSER_INIT_SCRIPTS and .agent-browser/config.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the child env from an allowlist (PATH, plus a scratch HOME and XDG dirs from mkdtemp), drop every inherited AGENT_BROWSER_* variable except EXECUTABLE_PATH, and remove the scratch HOME afterwards.
findings.preconditions: A developer has agent-browser configuration in the environment or HOME.

votes.reasoning: scripts/gen-orca-snapshot-fixtures.mjs:93 builds env = { ...process.env, AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH: chromium } and passes it to execFile(process.execPath, [AB_LAUNCHER, '--session', session, ...]) at :97. HOME is not overridden, no --config is passed, and cwd is inherited. The pinned agent-browser README documents that it reads AGENT_BROWSER_INIT_SCRIPTS (README:550, :1053), AGENT_BROWSER_PROFILE (:1048), AGENT_BROWSER_AUTO_CONNECT (:1078), AGENT_BROWSER_CONFIG (:1097) and ~/.agent-browser/config.json as user-level defaults (:1175). Ambient configuration therefore reaches the runs that produce the committed scripts/fixtures/orca-snapshot/<page>.json references. The actor is the developer's own shell and HOME, not an outside attacker. The main effect is fixture reproducibility, not a privilege boundary. A contaminated fixture would most likely make verify-orca-browser-snapshot-live fail with a false red rather than pass with a false green, though that depends on what the injection changes. One step cannot be settled statically: whether AUTO_CONNECT takes precedence over the explicit AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH and attaches to the user's running Chrome. The INIT_SCRIPTS and config.json paths apply as documented.
